bug_semantics: js_atomics_store and js_atomics_op (and the other Atomics ops that share that pointer-cache pattern) call js_atomics_get_ptr, which returns a raw pointer into a TypedArray's ArrayBuffer. They then convert argv[2] with JS_ToIntegerFree / JS_ToUint32 / JS_ToBigInt*, which can run attacker-controlled JS via valueOf. That JS can rab.resize() a resizable ArrayBuffer; js_array_buffer_resize js_realloc()s the backing store (freeing the old allocation) and updates TypedArray views, but does not set abuf->detached. After conversion the atomics code only re-checks abuf->detached, then performs atomic_store / atomic_fetch_* on the stale pointer — heap use-after-free. PoC: new ArrayBuffer(1024, {maxByteLength: ...}); Atomics.store/add(i32, 0, {valueOf(){ rab.resize(0); return 123; }}). Detach-during-conversion was already handled; resize-without-detach was not.
flaw_origin: The Atomics pointer-cache-then-convert pattern existed before resizable ArrayBuffers and was not a UAF then, because detach was re-validated after conversion and buffers could not otherwise move. PR #646 first implemented RABs with realloc-based resize and updated TypedArray prototype methods for valueOf-driven resize, but left Atomics unchanged. The smallest first-write is member 878647e21dec1a101a5d7ced6134e70a8e2ffca8 (parent e569f39bf18b4670dd526b11ea09cd00d7be3e91 has no js_array_buffer_resize / maxByteLength). GitHub squash-merged that PR as 37fe427d59043d70f92c70d315592232ad8cb358 onto master; later PR fixups did not touch atomics. The UAF remains through v0.11.0 until ea3e9d77454e8fc9cb3ef3c504e9c16af5a80141 re-resolves the pointer after conversion.
